winner.title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice With Fried Onions)

evidence.authenticity: Traditional method: par-cooked lentils, deeply browned onions as the base, rice cooked in the lentil liquid, optional fried onion topping. Intro frames it as a Levantine staple and mentions the bulgur variant. Author is a respected Persian-American cookbook author, not Levantine.
evidence.precision: No gram weights. Sized produce is limited to 'large' onions. 12-inch lidded pan, oil at 350F, 1 inch oil depth, rice rinsed until water runs clear. Sensory cues in 9 spots (lentils al dente, onions golden at edges then rich golden brown, liquid absorbed, rest 10 min).
evidence.testing: NYT Cooking test process. 889 ratings averaging 5 stars. Explains why to cook onions without stirring, why to save the lentil cooking water, and why to check lentils often so they do not overcook.
evidence.photos: Hidden behind the login and not marked down. Schema shows no step images; page has 46 images, unverified.
evidence.efficiency: Lentils and onions run in parallel, and the fried topping is made while the pot cooks. Stated total of 2 hours is slightly long, with 55 to 60 minutes of onion browning.
evidence.access: Everything is at a US grocery. Lentil type is flexible.

winner.why: It gives the most precise method (pan size, oil temperature, doneness cues, reserved lentil water) and has 889 five-star ratings, ahead of Cookie and Kate, which uses brown rice.

runnerUp.title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions)

evidence.authenticity: Calls it a classic Arabic dish, but the default is brown basmati and the recipe adds garlic, bay and green onions. Author is not from the cuisine.
evidence.precision: No gram weights. 12-inch skillet, medium-to-large onions, sensory cues in 7 steps (onions sizzle test, deeply caramelized and crisping at edges).
evidence.testing: Blogger-tested, 4.7 stars over 314 ratings. Includes notes on rice and lentil options and the towel-covered rest.
evidence.photos: Page has 52 images, but I could not confirm process photos because WebFetch returned 403. Schema shows no step images.
evidence.efficiency: Rice and lentils cook together while the onions brown. Stated 1 hour total is realistic.
evidence.access: All ingredients are at a US grocery.

runnerUp.why: Slightly less traditional because it uses brown rice, and its precision cues are weaker than the NYT recipe.

searches: Mujadara recipe lentils rice caramelized onions
notes: No recipe lists gram weights. The Mediterranean Dish version uses black lentils and a 40 minute onion browning. Food Network's version adds cinnamon, cayenne and pine nuts, which departs from the classic. Other NYT versions seen but not read: One-Pot Mujadara With Leeks and Greens (Melissa Clark, 2632 ratings, a variation), Bulgur Mujadara (Reem Kassis, 256 ratings, bulgur variant by a Palestinian author). Reem Kassis' bulgur version may suit if a more Levantine author is wanted. The Food Network and Mediterranean Dish scores are my estimates from the schema and not from page photos.
